scope: Independent read-only review of proposed wider GPU qualification orchestration; no compiler, GPU, VM or application execution

findings.problem: Declared provenance is not fully enforced. SOURCE-MANIFEST.json is read without verifying full_source_manifest.sha256. root_acceptance is unused. Build command records, shader command record, interface helper, copied codegen inputs and reused external rlibs are not checked against accepted evidence. A changed manifest/command/dependency can silently rebind the build while preserving the candidate manifest string.
findings.required_fix: Verify every consumed manifest and command/helper/dependency against hashes rooted in accepted immutable evidence before running compilers; verify full-source manifest hash in both stages. Record exact command and dependency hashes in build bindings. Keep outputs private.

findings.problem: New fallback binaries embed the current SPV files without requiring the accepted full/fallback shader hashes. The final embedding check only finds the current file bytes; it does not prove equality to the previously accepted pair or native reused binaries.
findings.required_fix: Read hash-pinned qualified manifest, assert both SPV SHA256 values before compilation, recheck afterward, and require every binary embedding record to contain the same accepted pair. GPU stage must verify the expected binding hashes before initialization.

findings.problem: The claimed exact8b baseline host renderer is compiled directly from the immutable-named directory without hashing its renderer source closure against an immutable8b manifest. baseline_archive_sha256 is copied from input text into output evidence. Only staged shader/shared code receives explicit baseline checks. Extra retained mixed-format guard input hash and staged workspace Cargo.toml hash are also never enforced.
findings.required_fix: Bind and check the complete baseline renderer/shared/font/shader source closure before and after compile against immutable8b evidence, including staged workspace manifest. Enforce all extra guard source hashes. Record verified baseline source-manifest/archive provenance rather than a copied label.

current_read_only_checks.feature_off_only_delta: gpu.rs request_device optional dual-source mask plus identity/feature diagnostics; other source files byte-identical

nonblocking_assessments: All explicit output/codegen/target paths are private under gpu-qualification; no canonical source, shader pair or shared target write was found in reviewed commands. Candidate/native executables remain read-only inputs.

Baseline expected failure requires exit101, RGB mismatch with preserved alpha37, numeric diagnostic and one failed/zero ignored summary; timeout, crash, validation/device errors and unexpected pass reject. Candidate tiny expected bytes remain255/255/255 with alpha37/241/254.

Core23 fixture inventory is unchanged and run twice, native plus feature-disabled, with worker/mixed-format/strict-subpixel/Direct/cache-off/generic555 guards retained. Inventory suppression is rejected and sanitized to0; capture variables are removed by TILE_RENDER_ environment sanitization.

Feature-off copy genuinely disables DUAL_SOURCE_BLENDING at request_device and logs actual enabled=false; renderer shader module selection uses actual device.features, so a passing same-adapter capability record can establish fallback SPV use after provenance fixes. Native available-dual inference relies on hash-pinned production optional_features/request_device and same-adapter fixture output.

Each diagnostic GPU fixture has a120s timeout and one test thread, with serial orchestration and hash-preserved logs/results. There are61 invocations, giving a worst-case cumulative diagnostic bound of122minutes if every test nearly times out. This is not a short broker lease; schedule accordingly. CPU compilation subprocesses have no timeout. No new production wait, lock, cap or resource policy is introduced.
Only logs/hash records are retained; strict fixture byte/oracle assertions remain unchanged. Numerical qualification does not establish App/runtime/Metal/performance/adoption acceptance.
